subject: Plot item function of a single dimension (general factor) of a mirt

messages.author: adb7c594d8eb78f0
messages.subject: Plot item function of a single dimension (general factor) of a mirt
parts:
Hey Phil,

I've been working with your MIRT package and I love it!

I've fit a four-dimensional, exploratory mirt model. Because I am assuming there is a general factor, I've rotated the model with the "bifactorQ" rotation (I guess in the end my model is similar to a bifactor model. However, it is exploratory compared to the bfactor() function MIRT offers). Because multiple dimensions are hard to plot I want to plot only the item information in regard to the general factor. I've been using the following code to get the information I need:

Theta <- matrix(seq(-6,6, by = .1))

Theta4 <- as.matrix(expand.grid(Theta,0,0,0))

extr <- extract.item(mod,item=i)

tmp <- iteminfo(extr, Theta4, degrees = c(0,90,90,90))

tmp <- data.frame(Theta4, info=tmp) 

Unfortunately, extract.item() cannot handle the bifactorQ rotation and thus, the values I get disregard the rotation. Is there another solution to this problem?

Cheers, Kornelius

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Plot item function of a single dimension (general factor) of a mirt
parts:
This is a bit harder. Given the rotation coefficients aren't really stored anywhere useful, and instead only returned after requested, you'd basically have to create an entirely new model with these new post-rotation coefficients. So something along the lines of 

bimod <- mirt(...)
cfs <- coef(bimod, rotate = 'bifactorQ')
sv <- mod2values(bimod)
sv$est <- FALSE
## set all elements of sv equal to those from the cfs output
....
newbimod <- mirt(..., pars = sv)

Then continue on with your usual approach. Certainly a hacky way to do the job, but what you're asking for is a little on the odd side. HTH.

Phil
